case_facts_html:
Fly Ltd. made a sale of INR 7,00,000 to Wings International in May 2023 and recognised Trade Receivables which was initially recorded at the prevailing exchange rate on the date of sales, transaction recorded at US$ 1= ₹79.4. The Company also took a loan from U.S Company for ₹10,00000 in December 2023 which was initially recorded at the prevailing exchange rate on the date of transaction, transaction recorded at US$ 1= ₹81.1.

On 31st March 2024, exchange rate was US$ 1 = ₹83.3.
question_html: What will be the closing balance of Trade Receivables on 31st March 2024:
answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹7,34,383 approx — the trade receivable is a foreign-currency monetary asset, restated at the closing rate on the balance sheet date. USD principal = ₹7,00,000 / 79.4 = USD 8,815.82 (approx); at the closing rate of USD 1 = ₹83.3, the restated balance = 8,815.82 × 83.3 = ₹7,34,383 approx.
chapter_label: AS 11: The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
topic_text: AS 11 (3.4): Foreign currency monetary item (trade receivable) restated at the closing rate on the balance sheet date
